metadata.note: The Chicago, Burlington & Quincy's original Chicago-Omaha main line, the eastern gateway to the Union Pacific's transcontinental route (see first_transcontinental_railroad.geojson for the Omaha-Promontory Summit segment) and the direct ancestor of the Exposition Flyer/California Zephyr corridor (see california_zephyr_historical.geojson, which picks up this same physical line in 1939). Route geometry is taken from the modern Amtrak California Zephyr's own GTFS-sourced alignment for this corridor (see amtrak.geojson), sliced to the Chicago-Omaha portion, since the historical CB&Q line ran the same physical route. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from a real timetable.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Burlington and Missouri River Railroad, Chicago Burlington and Quincy Railroad, Union Pacific Missouri River Bridge, Denver Zephyr), trains.com Burlington Route history, streamlinermemories.info (The Aristocrat)
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.coverage_correction: 2026-08-30: this feature was drawn 1870-1939 only, on the reasoning that california_zephyr_historical.geojson 'picks up this same physical line in 1939'. That layer carries company 'CB&Q / Rio Grande / Western Pacific' and colour #674ea7, so from 1939 the Burlington's own colour vanished from its own busiest main line even though the Denver, Nebraska, Ak-Sar-Ben and Kansas City Zephyrs all ran Chicago-Omaha under CB&Q colours until 1970. Segments 1939-1970 (CB&Q) and 1970-1971 (Burlington Northern) added. This is an understatement fix, not a Rule 1 overstatement. Source: research/branches/chicago_burlington_and_quincy_railroad.txt, EXISTING LAYER CHECK.

segments.note: The Burlington & Missouri River RR reached the Missouri River opposite Omaha in 1869-70 (via its Iowa Division and the Omaha & South Western acquisition), but through travel required a ferry crossing at Council Bluffs until the Union Pacific's Missouri River Bridge opened; estimated, unsourced

segments.note: Streamliner era: the Pioneer Zephyr's celebrated dawn-to-dusk Denver-Chicago run (May 26 1934) launched the Burlington's Zephyr fleet on this corridor, followed by the twice-daily Denver Zephyr (1936). The Exposition Flyer joined the corridor in 1939 -- see california_zephyr_historical.geojson -- but it did NOT supersede the CB&Q's own trains, which is what the earlier note here implied and why this feature used to stop in 1939; frequency estimated, unsourced

segments.note: The CB&Q went on running its own Chicago - Omaha trains under its own name for another thirty-one years alongside the jointly-operated Exposition Flyer and California Zephyr: the Denver Zephyr, Nebraska Zephyr, Ak-Sar-Ben Zephyr and Kansas City Zephyr all worked this corridor to the 1970 merger. Added 2026-08-30 -- the feature previously stopped in 1939, handing the whole corridor to the multi-company California Zephyr layer and erasing the Burlington's own busiest main line for thirty-one years; frequency estimated, unsourced
sources: Segment-level: CB&Q passenger service over Chicago - Omaha in 1951 is confirmed by the Feb 1952 Official Guide, Burlington Lines Tables 6 and 21 (cached at research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt). The 1970 and 1971 dates are the Burlington Northern merger (2 March 1970) and Amtrak day (1 May 1971). The headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.
Feb 1952 Official Guide of the Railways, Burlington Lines section

segments.note: Merged into Burlington Northern 2 March 1970; Amtrak took the surviving intercity trains 1 May 1971 and still runs this corridor as the California Zephyr; frequency estimated, unsourced
